chapter: Leaving home: Fisk, Tulsa, Arkansas City
title: Junior college in Arkansas City
summary: With savings he enrolled in junior college in Arkansas City but money ran short when the clubs closed, though he sometimes played for Alligator in Ponca City.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So after you had your job, you'd already been indoctrinated into this on the whiskey and the tobacco. You turned off for a while.
Yes, that's true. And so then I decided. I said, "Well, I'm going to go to school." So I went to junior college.
But you thought (inaudible).
Well, I always had a -- wanted to go to school. I don't know why I had it, you know, but I did, and so I went to junior college.
Where was that?
This was still in the same town, Arkansas City.
How did you have the money?
He saved it.
Well, I had saved it, you see. I had worked, you know, and I had worked and I had saved my money and

so then I went on to junior college. But you see now, after you're in college about a year and a half, see, your money's running out, see? Because they close the town up and there was nowhere for me to play. Couldn't make no money nowhere, you know. And the only thing --
Well, by closed up, do you mean Prohibition had gotten the better of things? (Inaudible).
Yes, when they -- you know, they completely closed Babe Burton up and Lee Deere --
They'd gone on top of the booze.

Yeah, so that there was nobody operating and that's when I sometimes would go down to this town I was telling you about, Ponca City, and playing maybe one night a week or two nights for Alligator, you know.
How do you spell that, Ponca City?

P-o-n-c-a. Ponca City. And that's the reason, you know, I ran into that stuff down there. I'd go down and play maybe one or two nights for Alligator, but then I'd have to take the bus and go down and wait and catch another bus late in the morning and come back, you know?
What were you studying at this junior college?
Oh, just studying, just regular course, just regular college course.
You weren't sort of specialized in

Didn't specialize in anything. And it was a drawback because I didn't have any -- for me, what I wanted was an instrument, but I didn't have no instrument, so that was a drawback to me. Otherwise, I could have gotten into school, just with a school band, you know, which I really wanted to do. But sometimes I would borrow a fella's, he had a clarinet and I used to borrow his clarinet. And went over there to the school band, you know, but that didn't last too long because his folks made him bring his clarinet in, you know what I mean?
